summary: In this excerpt from Book 11 (part 108) of a novel, Miranda reports privately to Jane on Hannah's selfish, unreliable character, and says the farm mortgage will be cleared by Rebecca or herself rather than Hannah. Rebecca then arrives to tell Emma Jane that her essay Wareham Wildflowers has been accepted by The Pilot, to appear in the next issue. Emma Jane is overwhelmed, and the two girls dream of living together, but Rebecca notes that their hopes depend on paying off the mortgage, which has grown more burdensome since the interest went unpaid this year.
one_line: Rebecca tells Emma Jane her essay is accepted by The Pilot, and the two dream of a home while the family mortgage weighs on them.
key_facts: Miranda considers Hannah close as the bark of a tree and considerably selfish.
Miranda says Hannah would kick the ladder out from under her once she had climbed as far as she could in the world.
Miranda says that if the farm mortgage is ever cleared, it will be Rebecca or herself who clears it, not Hannah.
Rebecca tells Emma Jane that her contribution entitled Wareham Wildflowers has been accepted for The Pilot.
Rebecca says the senior editor read Wareham Wildflowers and thought it highly instructive.
Wareham Wildflowers appears in the next issue of The Pilot.
Emma Jane asks whether the piece appears in the same number as her poem about the golden gates that close behind us when we leave school.
Emma Jane says that if anything happens to her, she asks Rebecca solemnly to bury that number of The Pilot with her.
Rebecca says that whenever she takes out the Pilot back numbers to read her contributions, she almost bursts with pleasure.
Rebecca says her contributions look worse to her every time she reads them.
Emma Jane proposes that she and Rebecca live together in a little house, with Emma Jane doing the housework and cooking and copying the poems and stories.
Rebecca says she would like nothing better, but she has promised to keep house for John.
Rebecca says John will not have a house for a good many years unless they can pay off the detestable mortgage.
Rebecca says the mortgage day grows farther off now that the interest was not paid this year.
